alice.support: anyone seeing a spike in 502/504s for hosted api? customer reports streaming chat connections drop with 502 after ~45s, they attached trace id trace=abc1237
ben.sre: yep datadog shows edge_frontdoor_502 spike around that window, looks tied to long-lived http2 streams :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy completed auth-proxy v2.3.7 -> prod at 1711278700
carla.eng-infra: pulling envoy logs now — seeing repeated 'upstream reset before response' and 'http2: stream closed (id=13)'. upstream rtt is fine, but frontdoor shows early-close on h2 streams. possible keepalive/idle timeout mismatch
ben.sre: can you paste a customer repro curl? want to try locally against staging
alice.support: customer repro (from them): ```curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --data-binary @prompt.json "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream?model=gpt-neox-3.7b"``` they say it reliably 502s at ~48s when payloads are large and multiple concurrent streams exist
carla.eng-infra: reproducing in staging now. quick mitigation: bump frontdoor http2 idle_timeout to 90s and increase upstream max_concurrent_streams on the auth-proxy pool. also check nginx keepalive_pool on authcache nodes
ben.sre: seeing h2 SETTINGS/INITIAL_WINDOW smaller than prod in a few frontdoor instances; window updates are getting delayed under token burst which can look like stall -> auth-proxy resets stream. i'll dump envoy config and stats for those hosts
mike.oncall: applied canary config: frontdoor http2_idle_timeout=90s for 10% of traffic at 1711278980 — monitoring :eyes:
deploy-bot: config-rollout frontdoor canary 10% -> 1711278980
alice.support: customer reports better behavior when routed through canary path, but still occasional 502s under heavy concurrency. sent them a request to capture full curl -v logs and trace id trace=xyz789 when it happens
carla.eng-infra: dug into auth-proxy codepath: on certain backpressure/queue-timeout we do a hard stream close instead of graceful drain — that'll surface as 502 at the edge. i'll open a patch to return a 503 fallback or keep stream open while signaling backpressure
ben.sre: action items: 1) increase frontdoor idle_timeout to 90s globally (I can roll), 2) patch auth-proxy to avoid hard-closing h2 streams (carla owns), 3) add KB for customers about chunking large prompts and recommended chunk sizes (i'll own). ETA: global change within ~2h, auth-proxy PR in progress (4-6h), KB draft 24h
alice.support: thanks — i'll update the customer and mark this as escalated. will paste customer curl logs/trace ids here when they come in :thumbsup:
carla.eng-infra: opened PR 5123 with the change, added unit test for h2 drain behavior. linking logs and repro snippet in the PR description
ben.sre: once global change is rolled i'll run a 1k concurrent stream soak against staging to validate no regressions
alice.support: noted, keeping channel updated. if customer still sees failures after global change i'll ask for pcaps and full TRACE spans
_meta_note: This thread is a simulated Slack conversation for dataset purposes. Messages are short and contain realistic troubleshooting steps, logs, and commands.
